questions.scenario: An ARM template contains a parameter named skuName with a defaultValue of Standard_LRS and allowedValues of Standard_LRS and Standard_GRS. You deploy the template and pass skuName=Standard_GRS on the command line.
questions.question: Which SKU is used for the storage account?

options.text: Standard_GRS
options.why: Correct. A value supplied at deployment time overrides the defaultValue, and Standard_GRS is in the allowed list.

options.text: Standard_LRS
options.why: The defaultValue is used only when no value is supplied.

options.text: The deployment fails because the value differs from the default
options.why: Any value in allowedValues is valid. It does not need to match the default.

options.text: Standard_ZRS
options.why: Standard_ZRS is not referenced by the template or the deployment.

questions.explanation: Parameter values passed at deployment take precedence over default values. Values outside allowedValues fail validation.

questions.question: An ARM template sets the location of a resource to [resourceGroup().location]. You deploy the template to a resource group in West Europe while your Cloud Shell session runs in East US. Where is the resource created?

options.text: West Europe
options.why: Correct. resourceGroup().location returns the region of the target resource group.

options.text: East US
options.why: The location of the Cloud Shell session does not affect the template function.

options.text: The paired region of West Europe
options.why: The function returns the resource group region, not its pair.

options.text: The deployment fails because no location parameter is supplied
options.why: The expression provides the location, so no parameter is needed.

questions.explanation: resourceGroup().location is commonly used as the default location so that resources follow their resource group.

questions.scenario: An ARM template defines a skuName parameter with allowedValues of Standard_LRS and Standard_GRS. Administrators must be able to deploy storage accounts that use Standard_ZRS. The default must remain Standard_LRS.
questions.question: What should you modify in the template?

options.text: Add Standard_ZRS to the allowedValues array of the skuName parameter
options.why: Correct. Adding the value to allowedValues lets it pass validation while the defaultValue is unchanged.

options.text: Change the defaultValue of skuName to Standard_ZRS
options.why: This changes the default, which must remain Standard_LRS, and validation would still fail because the value is not allowed.

options.text: Add a variable named skuName with the value Standard_ZRS
options.why: A variable does not change which parameter values are accepted.

options.text: Add Standard_ZRS to the outputs section
options.why: Outputs return values after deployment and do not affect input validation.

questions.explanation: allowedValues restricts the accepted values for a parameter. Changing it does not alter the defaultValue.

questions.scenario: You maintain a Bicep file that deploys a virtual machine. The admin password is currently passed as a plain string parameter, and the VM size is hard-coded as 'Standard_D2s_v5' in the resource.
questions.question: Which two changes should you make so that the password is not shown in deployment history and administrators can choose the VM size at deployment time? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Add the @secure() decorator to the adminPassword parameter
options.why: Correct. @secure() prevents the value from being logged or returned in deployment history.

options.text: Add a vmSize parameter and use it for the hardwareProfile vmSize property
options.why: Correct. A parameter makes the size configurable at deployment time.

options.text: Move the password into a var declaration
options.why: Variables are part of the template and are not protected like secure parameters.

options.text: Add the password to an output
options.why: Outputs are stored in deployment history, which exposes the password.

options.text: Rename the resource symbolic name to vmSize
options.why: The symbolic name only identifies the resource inside the file and does not create a parameter.

questions.explanation: Use @secure() (securestring in ARM JSON) for secrets, and replace hard-coded values with parameters.

questions.question: A Bicep file contains the following line: resource st 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts@2023-05-01' = { name: storageName ... }. Another resource in the same file references st.id. What does st represent?

options.text: The symbolic name used to reference the storage account inside the Bicep file
options.why: Correct. The symbolic name is used for references, and Bicep infers the dependency from it.

options.text: The name of the storage account in Azure
options.why: The Azure resource name comes from the name property, which is storageName.

options.text: A parameter that the user must supply
options.why: Parameters are declared with the param keyword.

options.text: An output returned after deployment
options.why: Outputs are declared with the output keyword.

questions.explanation: Bicep symbolic names replace resourceId() and dependsOn in most cases. The name property sets the actual resource name.
